rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation changes > to >= in max comparison. This affects only WHICH index stores the max (first vs last occurrence of duplicate maxima), not the max VALUE itself. Since return_indices=False is hardcoded, only max_val is returned. For any window values, final max_val is identical in both versions (the true maximum), so output tensors are always bitwise identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the behavior from selecting the first occurrence of the maximum value to selecting the last occurrence when duplicates exist within a pooling window. However, the actual maximum VALUE computed is always identical between original and mutant. Since the Python code hardcodes return_indices=False, only the output tensor containing max_val values is returned, while the indices tensor (where the behavioral difference manifests) is never allocated or returned. The internal state difference in max_index cannot propagate to any observable output.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the current configuration. The only way to kill it would be to change return_indices to True, which would require modifying the Python code (not just input values). Under the fixed contract with return_indices=False, no input values can produce different outputs.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing kernels with multiple outputs (like max pooling with optional indices), ensure tests cover ALL output modes. This mutant would be trivially killed if return_indices=True were tested. Consider adding configuration-level mutation coverage that varies boolean flags like return_indices, not just input tensor values.
